transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-09-03 10:00 UTC
Duration: ~46 minutes
Attendees: Sam Ortiz (Redwood AE), Priya Kapoor (Redwood SE), Liam Chen (Bluewell CTO), Maya Patel (Bluewell ML Eng), Rajiv Suri (Bluewell Product)

Summary:
- Week 3 readout comparing Redwood pilot against incumbent baseline on latency and throughput. Redwood shows better p95 in most routing configs; baseline better in sustained token/s at one large batch point.
- Action: share raw CSVs, provision dedicated slots, run traffic replay against baseline, schedule VPC/KMS deep-dive.

Topics: benchmark numbers, routing/quantization tradeoffs, KV cache warmup, cost delta, SLO fallback, security constraints (VPC/KMS/SOC2).

Transcript body:
[00:00] Sam Ortiz: hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick check — can you hear okay?
[00:03] Liam Chen: yeah loud and clear, thanks. we got the bench deck, excited to go through the numbers.
[00:08] Priya Kapoor: great, i'll run through the readout, i'll call out assumptions up front — model variant is rw-13b-quant8 (simulated), sequence length 256 median, traffic fixture is mixture of short prompts and 1-2 long queries.
[00:20] Maya Patel: just to confirm, the baseline runs we provided earlier were 13b fp16 on IncumbentCloudAI with their autoscale config, right?
[00:26] Sam Ortiz: correct, and we re-ran with your logs to align windows — couple notes on sample variance, but numbers should be comparable.
[00:33] Priya Kapoor: okay the headline p95: Redwood pilot measured about 78ms p95 for short prompts, baseline reported ~120ms p95 under same fixture. p50's are similar — 22ms vs 28ms. p99 however is closer, 340ms vs 400ms but that is with cold kv cache in both.
[00:50] Rajiv Suri: 78ms p95 is great — what's the token throughput? if we go to production we need sustained tps of at least 4000 tokens/sec.
[00:58] Priya Kapoor: we saw peak token throughput ~6.8k tokens/s on a 4-GPU Dedicated slot with continuous batching and prefix cache. sustained at 4k tokens/s was reliable when batch windows set to 40–60ms. baseline peaked at 7.5k in a single large batch test but its sustained under our mixed fixture fell to ~3.5k because of longer queueing lat spikes.
[01:20] Liam Chen: hmm so the baseline wins peak single-case but loses on mixed realistic workloads. can you explain why the sustained dropped?
[01:25] Priya Kapoor: yeah it's mostly queueing and how their autoscaler opens larger batch windows which increases tail latency for short prompts. ours uses workload-aware continuous batching and KV prefix caching so short prompts often hit p95 low. the tradeoff is if you force very large batch sizes you'll see higher aggregated throughput but worse latency for interactive calls.
[01:43] Maya Patel: curious about quantization — your run used quant8? how confident are you that quality's consistent vs fp16? we had a couple hallucination flags in earlier small-sample evals.
[01:52] Sam Ortiz: good point — we ran our standard eval set against the quantized variant and the delta was within your threshold (BLEU/ROUGE style proxies) for 97% of the prompts. priya, you want to add on the evals?
[01:59] Priya Kapoor: yes, we observed a slight increase in repetition on long-form generative tests, but for your product's majority short-response traffic the quality delta was negligible. we can push an A/B with a small sample to be safe.
[02:12] Rajiv Suri: costs? we need unit economics — per-1M tokens numbers. baseline said $X but their number looked amortized differently.
[02:18] Sam Ortiz: so from our lab the all-in unit cost at your observed mix is about 30% lower for Redwood when using Dedicated with autoscale and KV caching enabled — this includes GPU runtime, bandwidth, and our routing overhead. i'll put raw calc in the sheet.
[02:30] Maya Patel: can you share the raw logs? we want to run the same fixture ourselves against the baseline to validate.
[02:35] Priya Kapoor: yes, we'll attach the fixture and a step-by-step playback guide. note: to reproduce p95 you need the same concurrency profile and same batch window settings. small changes there change tails a lot.
[02:46] Liam Chen: there was a spike in p99 around 21:40 in your logs — what caused that?
[02:50] Priya Kapoor: i looked at that — it matches a KV cache miss storm during a cold-start window. when the workload changed pattern we saw a few seconds where many requests warmed new prefixes simultaneously. we have two mitigations: proactive cache prefill for known prefixes and fallback routing to a slightly larger model variant during warmup.
[03:07] Rajiv Suri: fallback routing — that sounds complex. how do you manage correctness and cost if it routes to larger variants?
[03:12] Sam Ortiz: it's policy driven — you can set SLO thresholds and cost ceilings. we do canary fallback to a compatibility variant and you can set a budget for how often to allow fallback. we also emit tracing and tagging so you can filter those requests in analytics.
[03:25] Maya Patel: security and compliance — we need info about audit logs retention and KMS integration. our legal flagged SOC2 and KMS artifacts as must-haves.
[03:33] Priya Kapoor: Redwood Private supports customer-managed KMS and HSM integrations; we produce audit logs per token-level request id and store them according to retention policy. for the pilot we can provide a tailored retention config and sample audit artifacts.
[03:45] Liam Chen: for VPC, what's the network topology? can we bring our own VPC or do you create peered subnet?
[03:51] Sam Ortiz: you can do either. Dedicated supports VPC peering, and Private includes a full bring-your-own-VPC flow. we'll schedule a short topology session next week.
[03:58] Rajiv Suri: any surprises or known limitations from the week 3 runs?
[04:02] Priya Kapoor: nothing blocker-level. items to note: cache cold-starts, slight quality delta on long-form with quant8, and we saw a small number of degraded runs when concurrency spiked above configured upper bound — those were mitigated by autoscale bump but we'd like to test dedicated reserved capacity for your SLAs.
[04:21] Maya Patel: can you re-run with the 'stress short prompt' fixture that biases toward sub-64 token replies? that is our dominant pattern.
[04:27] Priya Kapoor: absolutely — we'll run that on the dedicated slot and share results.
[04:30] Sam Ortiz: to recap next steps quickly — we will share the raw CSV and cost calc, provision dedicated test slots starting Friday, Maya will run baseline replay and upload logs, and we'll schedule the VPC/KMS call.
[04:40] Liam Chen: sounds good. timeline we have internally is decision by Sept 15, so those dates line up.
[04:46] Sam Ortiz: perfect, thanks all. we'll follow up in email with links.

End of call.
